evidence: Clear separation into models (models.py), views (views/classroom.py, students.py, teachers.py), and templates (templates/)
Django's built-in class-based views (ListView, CreateView, UpdateView, etc.) follow MVC convention where views handle request logic and templates handle presentation
Views import models and forms, and render templates—classic MVC flow
URL routing (urls.py) maps endpoints to view classes/functions, decoupling routing from business logic
Models define domain entities (User, Quiz, Question, etc.) with business logic and persistence concerns
Directory structure organizes concerns per app (classroom/) with subcomponents for models, views, templates—typical Django MVC pattern
risks: Tight coupling between Django ORM models and views through forms and decorators could reduce testability
View layer is more active than in strict MVC (e.g., business logic in views like login() + transaction decorators), bordering on Active Record anti-pattern in places
